title: Indefinite causal order with output-signalling instruments
authors: Ricardo Silveira, Patrick Andriolo, Davide Poderini, Dmitry Melnikov, Rafael Chaves
abstract: Quantum processes can exhibit indefinite causal order, allowing coherent superpositions of distinct orderings of events. Whether such processes generate genuinely noncausal statistics, however, depends not only on their global causal structure but also on the local operations available to the parties. Here, we restrict communication to the classical outcomes of local operations, yielding a causal polytope with new causal inequalities that can be violated using measure-and-reprepare, entanglement-breaking instruments requiring no coherent transmission through the laboratories. Using a semidefinite-programming framework, we bound the achievable violations and reveal noncausal correlations that satisfy all conventional input-signalling inequalities, demonstrating that restricting the information available for communication can uncover forms of indefinite causal order inaccessible under less restrictive operational assumptions.
summary: This work explores indefinite causal order in quantum processes under the constraint that communication is limited to classical measurement outcomes. By using semidefinite programming, the authors derive a new, tighter causal polytope for this 'output-signalling' scenario. This demonstrates that restricting local operations can uncover forms of noncausal correlations previously hidden from conventional causal witnesses.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum processes exhibiting indefinite causal order (ICO) when communication is restricted to classical outcomes of local operations (output-signalling instruments).
main_result: Restricting communication to output-signalling defines a new causal polytope with unique inequalities that can reveal noncausal correlations inaccessible under standard input-signalling assumptions.
method: The analysis uses a semidefinite-programming framework to geometrically characterize the achievable correlations and derive the facet-defining inequalities for the output-signalling causal polytope.
model_or_system: The model is a bipartite quantum system involving two parties (A and B) in semi-isolated laboratories, where local operations are restricted to entanglement-breaking 'measure-and-reprepare' instruments.
key_observables: The achievable correlations, represented by joint probability distributions p(a, b|x, y), and the violation of derived causal inequalities (e.g., I1 to I38).
important_parameters: The restriction to classical outcomes of local operations, which defines the specific causal polytope.
main_assumptions: Communication is strictly limited to the classical outcomes of local measurements, prohibiting coherent transmission of input settings.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the setup for ICO and measure-and-reprepare instruments; Figure 2 illustrates the difference between input-signalling and output-signalling communication models.
paper_structure: The paper compares the output-signalling scenario to the input-signalling scenario, details the mathematical framework using semidefinite programming, and presents the resulting set of causal inequalities.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, operational constraint (output-signalling) that tightens the bounds on quantum correlations, offering a new tool to certify non-classicality beyond standard input-signalling tests.
